Yes, you can freeze cooked rice. Let it cool to room temperature within an hour of cooking, then portion it into airtight containers or freezer bags. Flatten the bags so the rice freezes evenly and thaws faster. Frozen rice keeps for about a month. To reheat, microwave it with a splash of water, covered, until it is steaming hot all the way through.

The fall of the Western Roman Empire in 476 CE was the result of a complex combination of factors rather than a single event. Economic troubles, including heavy taxation and inflation, weakened the state from within. At the same time, military pressures from Germanic tribes and the Huns strained the empire's resources. Political instability, marked by frequent changes in leadership, further undermined effective governance. Together, these challenges created a situation in which the empire could no longer sustain itself.

Studying effectively is less about how many hours you put in and more about how you use them. Active recall, where you test yourself instead of rereading notes, is one of the most effective techniques backed by research. Spaced repetition helps move information into long-term memory. It's also important to take regular breaks and get enough sleep, as both play a key role in memory consolidation. By incorporating these strategies, you can study smarter, not harder.
